title: Taking “you are here” to a whole new level- seeing Come From Away in ...
transcript: Let me tell you, seeing Come From Away in the city, where it actually took place, is unlike anything I have ever experienced before. I got to fly out to Gander, Newfoundland, spend some time exploring the town and meeting some of the people that inspired the show. And all of that culminated in me seeing the gander production of Come From Away. This is their fourth summer doing it, and it is a completely new production and staging and taking a ton of inspiration from Gander itself. So, for example, the floor of the stage resembles a clock that hangs in the Gander airport. And the set and theatre are aligned with these little quilted patches. They were actually made by Newfoundlanders who were around during this period. The director actually came out before the show and told us that they originally just wanted enough to cover that back wall, but in true Newfoundland fashion, ended up getting so many sent in that they ended up lining the walls of the theatre with them as well. Which to me, served as yet another reminder of just how giving this community is. It's obviously a major theme of the show, but just getting to experience it all firsthand was so special. And what was really interesting about seeing this show with an audience of predominantly Canadians and Newfoundlanders was seeing them react to specific references that didn't really get any reaction in New York. As well as just being in Gander, For a few days, and hearing the names of locations that I had visited or stories that I had heard recounted, it was like seeing the show through fresh eyes. The other really cool thing about this production is that there are two returning Broadway cast members, as well as two returning musicians from the Broadway pit. Those cast members are Petrina Bromley, who played Bonnie in the original Broadway cast, but here is playing the role of Beverly. She herself is actually a newfoundlander, and it was really cool to get to see her in a completely new role. And the other is Josh Breckenridge, who was a swing in the original Broadway company, and here is playing the role of Bob. and he is just finding so many new, delicious line readings in this track, and I think he might be having the most fun out of anyone on that stage. But honestly, the entire cast was really great. It is predominantly Canadian and I believe about half Newfoundlanders, and that authenticity really shines through. And while the original production feels like a love letter to this community, this production feels like a love letter from this community. They're not just patting themselves on the back and saying, look at this great thing we did, but instead commemorating this moment of time with humility and gratitude, recognizing all of the good that came out of this horrific event.
